subject: Re: EaseMed — UK IDTA, TIA scope, and subprocessor inventory
messages:
From: Elsa Grant <elsa@easemed.health>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: EaseMed Legal <privacy@easemed.health>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EaseMed onboarding — transfer safeguards and UK-specific ask

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — the team liked the latency profiles and the Dedicated options. We are starting legal intake for production onboarding and need to confirm a few things before we proceed to IT and procurement:

1) UK customers: we handle patient contact data and will be signing the UK Addendum / IDTA. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to the standard UK IDTA terms (including the UK Addendum where needed)?

2) TIA/DTIA scope: our privacy team needs a short scoping note that outlines what a Transfer Impact Assessment would cover for workloads routed through Redwood's EU region and for the UK Addendum case (routing to GB-hosted instances).

3) Subprocessors: please provide the current subprocessor inventory + locations and indicate any planned changes in the next 90 days. SOC2 reports and the latest SCC/TIA mapping are helpful.

We attach a template subprocessor CSV (we filled a few rows) — please populate and return. If easier, point us to a drive folder with the artifacts.

Can we aim to close the legal checklist by next Tuesday (21 Sep)?

Best,
Elsa
Director of Compliance
EaseMed Health

Attachments: easemed-subprocessors-20270914.csv (template)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elsa Grant <elsa@easemed.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EaseMed onboarding — transfer safeguards and UK-specific ask

Hi Elsa — great to hear and thanks for the clear checklist. Quick responses inline and next steps below.

1) UK Addendum/IDTA: Redwood supports the UK Addendum and we can execute the standard IDTA flow. For production we typically require: a) the customer to select UK-hosted private deployments (or Dedicated capacity pinned to UK region) and b) an executed UK Addendum. We can accept minor fill-in redlines but material changes to liability or data residency may need legal review.

2) TIA/DTIA scoping note: I pulled a short draft TIA scope that maps our ingestion, transient KV caches, logging retention, and subprocessor routing. I'll attach a one-page draft and loop in Marissa for legal/TIA specifics.

3) Subprocessors: attached is our current inventory CSV exported from the contract portal; I added columns for region and SOC/attestation. Kimberly will confirm any planned changes.

Next steps:
- Kimberly: confirm if any subprocessor changes expected in next 90 days and confirm SOC2 availability for infra processors.
- Marissa / Legal: once we finalize the TIA scope I'll prepare an acceptance note and the UK Addendum draft (we maintain a 1-page differ summary for customers).
- Elsa: once you confirm the scope items we can route DocuSign for the UK Addendum and provide the evidence bundle.

Can we set a 30-min call Thursday (16 Sep) to walk the privacy team through the scope?

Thanks,
Jonas
Head of Privacy & Compliance (Sales Enablement)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: easemed-subprocessors-20270914.csv (populated), proposed-uk-addendum-diff-jonas-20270917.pdf (placeholder)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EaseMed onboarding — transfer safeguards and UK-specific ask

Folks — quick update from ops/legal ops:

- Subprocessors: no major vendor changes planned in the next 90 days; one upcoming minor upgrade for our metrics pipeline that will introduce a managed telemetry aggregator (hosted in EU). I will flag that with customers classified as "monitoring" subprocessor.
- SOC2: we have the latest SOC2 Type II (infra + production) available; I'll upload to the secure drive link and share per-customer access.
- Data routing: for UK Addendum cases we offer either dedicated UK pools (customer-managed VPC) or a routing tag that pins requests to GB regions. The TIA needs to capture both: (a) logical routing + (b) whether customer elects Dedicated / Private.

Action items:
- Marissa: please take lead on TIA content and confirm any limitations for health/PD data.
- Jonas: I'll prepare a short bullet summary of subprocessor controls for the customer-facing TIA appendix.

-Kimberly
Director, Infrastructure Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elsa Grant <privacy@easemed.health>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EaseMed onboarding — transfer safeguards and UK-specific ask

Hi Elsa, Jonas — following our internal sync I attached a short draft TIA scope document that maps the transfer flows we discussed. Highlights: 

- Scope covers: request routing (EU vs GB), model hosting locations, transient KV cache retention (max 8 hours by default), token-level logs (retained 30 days, can be configured), and subprocessor list by function (infra, telemetry, analytics).
- Preliminary risk note: when routing to GB-hosted Dedicated pools, residual risk for cross-border access is low if customer requires Private deployment + customer-managed KMS. We'll flag any exceptions where on-call vendor access could require cross-border support.
- Evidence bundle: SOC2 link + subprocessor CSV + network topology diagram.

Elsa — can you review and confirm if this scope satisfies EaseMed's internal checklist or whether you need deeper controls (e.g., no telemetry aggregator permitted)? If it's good, Jonas can issue the UK Addendum via DocuSign and we can attach the evidence bundle.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: tia-scope-draft-20270920.docx

Subject: Re: EaseMed onboarding — transfer safeguards and UK-specific ask

Marissa / team — thanks for the fast turnaround. Reviewed the TIA draft and the subprocessor inventory. A few quick notes: 

- The telemetry aggregator flagged as "monitoring" is acceptable provided we receive a data minimization attestation and the aggregator is restricted to metrics-only (no raw payloads).
- For UK Addendum: EaseMed confirms we will elect Dedicated UK-hosted pools and require customer-managed KMS. Please proceed with the standard UK Addendum and routing config.
- DocuSign: prefer the addendum and the standard DPA clause set to be bundled; please share the link.

If you can send the DocuSign by EOD Wednesday (22 Sep) we'll route for signatures and aim for provisioning the Dedicated pool the following week.

Best regards,
Elsa
Director of Compliance
EaseMed Health
